title: Polynomial-presentation model for the affine small-etale naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $T$ a set, $P=R[x_t\mid t\in T]$ a polynomial algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\alpha:P\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism. Set $I=\ker\alpha$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], viewed as schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $V\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and view $U\to V$ (induced by $R\to B$) as a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Regard $I/I^2$ as a $B=P/I$-module. Put $E^{-1}=I/I^2$, $E^0=B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$, and $d([h])=1\otimes\mathrm dh$, with zero terms outside degrees $-1,0$. Differentials mean [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The Leibniz rule makes $d$ well-defined and $B$-linear. For a $B$-module $M$, denote by $M^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}$ the associated small-etale module sheaf of the Zariski quasi-coherent sheaf $\widetilde M$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections, def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Then there is an isomorphism
$$\mathrm{NL}_{U/V}\simeq[(I/I^2)^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{d^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}}(B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}})$$
[def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No finiteness, Noetherian, flatness or regular-sequence hypothesis is imposed on $R\to B$, $T$ or $I$.

source.place: Tag 0D0X, lemma-NL-compare-spaces-schemes; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0D0I, lemma-NL-affine; algebra.tex Tag 00S1, lemma-NL-homotopy, polynomial-presentation comparison. Associated small-etale sheaves as in descent.tex Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Write $E$ for the displayed module complex and $C=C_{B/R}$ for the canonical presentation complex in [lem-sfb-zariski-naive-cotangent-affine-comparison]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentations-homotopy-equivalent] to $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $R[x_b\mid b\in B]\twoheadrightarrow B$, $x_b\mapsto b$. Its maps $\varphi=(\varphi_1,\varphi_0):E\to C$ and $\psi=(\psi_1,\psi_0):C\to E$ commute with the differentials, and $h,h'$ are chain homotopies: $\mathrm{id}-\psi\varphi=hd+dh$ and $\mathrm{id}-\varphi\psi=h'd+dh'$, read in degrees $-1$ and $0$. Let $G(M)=M^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}=(\widetilde M)_{\mathrm{et}}$. It is the functor $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (a left adjoint, hence additive), landing in quasi-coherent modules by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], followed by the equivalence $F\mapsto F_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], which is the tensor pullback $\epsilon_U^*$ and so additive. Applying the additive functor $G$ termwise preserves all these identities, so $G(\varphi):G(E)\to G(C)$ is a chain homotopy equivalence of sheaf complexes, hence a quasi-isomorphism and an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}})$. Here $G(E)$ is exactly the two-term complex in the statement, with differential $d^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}=G(d)$. This uses arbitrary sets of generators, not finite presentations.

source.place: Tag 00S1, lemma-NL-homotopy, comparison with the canonical presentation

proof.text: The affine Zariski comparison [lem-sfb-zariski-naive-cotangent-affine-comparison] gives a quasi-isomorphism of complexes $\widetilde C\to\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}$. The tensor pullback $\epsilon_U^*$ is exact on all module sheaves by [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], so termwise pullback preserves this quasi-isomorphism. For each term $M$ of $C$, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies $\epsilon_U^*\widetilde M$ with $M^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}=G(M)$ naturally in $M$, since its forward functor is this tensor pullback. Naturality applied to the single differential identifies the complexes $\epsilon_U^*\widetilde C$ and $G(C)$, giving $G(C)\simeq\epsilon_U^*\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}})$.

source.place: Tag 0D0I, lemma-NL-affine; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08H8, lemma-epsilon-flat; descent.tex Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-naive-cotangent-etale-comparison] to the schemes $U,V$ and their representable algebraic spaces over the given $S$. It gives $\epsilon_U^*\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{U/V}$. Compose its inverse with the inverse of Step 2 and the inverse of the isomorphism $G(\varphi)$ of Step 1. The resulting isomorphism $\mathrm{NL}_{U/V}\simeq G(E)$ has as target exactly the two-term sheaf complex in the statement. All three comparisons retain degrees $-1,0$; no flatness of $I/I^2$ has been used.
